unit.title: Clinical Office Practice and Patient Safety

sections.learningObjectives:
- Recognize a sterile field and the conditions that keep it sterile.
- Avoid contaminating a sterile field by applying aseptic technique.
- Protect patient privacy during procedures and report contamination promptly to the appropriate person.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

A sterile field is like a freshly cleaned, germ-free 'safe zone' table where nothing dirty is allowed to touch.

### Question 2

Clean is 'washed,' but sterile is 'completely germ-free' - like hands that are rinsed versus hands that are truly disinfected.

### Question 3

Imagine a placemat: only the middle is germ-free; the outside edge is 'off-limits' because it might touch the table.

### Question 4

Only items still in their sealed, not-yet-expired 'germ-free wrapper' belong inside the safe zone.

### Question 5

It is like checking that a snack wrapper is not torn and not past its date before you open it.

### Question 6

Germs tend to hang out lower and where you cannot see, so keep the safe zone up high and in front of you.

### Question 7

Reaching over the safe zone is like shaking crumbs over a clean plate.

### Question 8

You cannot protect a clean plate if you cannot see it - so do not leave it alone.

### Question 9

A wet paper towel can let germs slip through - a wet shield no longer protects.

### Question 10

Germ-free only stays germ-free if it only touches other germ-free things.

### Question 11

If something dirty lands on the clean plate, you need a new plate - you cannot just pick it off.

### Question 12

Pick up the glove by its folded 'hem' so you do not dirty the part that will touch the patient.

### Question 13

Once one hand is germ-free, use it to help dress the other hand without touching anything dirty.

### Question 14

Open it like a present, away from you, so you do not lean over the germ-free inside.

### Question 15

Your breath has tiny germ droplets, so do not talk over the clean plate.

### Question 16

Fewer people walking by means less dust blowing onto the clean area.

### Question 17

Do not flap the clean cloth around - it blows dust onto it.

### Question 18

A soaked germ shield cannot block germs.

### Question 19

A good safe zone is dry, flat, made of germ-free cloth, and only holds germ-free items.

### Question 20

A ripped or damp wrapper means germs may have gotten in.

### Question 21

It is like closing the curtain when you change clothes so only what is needed is seen.

### Question 22

Cover everything except the part the provider needs to look at.

### Question 23

If it touched the floor, it is dirty no matter how clean it looks.

### Question 24

Pour carefully so the bottle never touches the clean cup, and tip a little out first to rinse the edge.

### Question 25

Use clean 'grabber' tools so your hands never touch the germ-free tool.

### Question 26

A hole in a raincoat lets rain in - replace it right away.

### Question 27

If you are not sure a plate is clean, get a clean plate.

### Question 28

Always knock and wait, like when a door is closed at home.

### Question 29

Only people who need to be there should be in the room.

### Question 30

Tell the person what is happening and keep them covered as much as possible.

### Question 31

Private information stays private - do not talk about it where others can hear.

### Question 32

Shut the door and curtain like you would at home.

### Question 33

Speak up right away if the clean zone got touched.

### Question 34

If you drop it, say so and get a clean one - do not hide it.

### Question 35

Tell the person in charge right away.

### Question 36

Write down what happened the way the office says to.

### Question 37

If no one kept an eye on the clean plate, get a fresh plate.

### Question 38

If it touches the 'off-limits' edge, it is no longer germ-free.

### Question 39

Walk around instead of reaching over the clean zone.

### Question 40

Loose things can accidentally dip into the clean area.

### Question 41

Clean your hands before touching the clean supplies.

### Question 42

Gloves are like a shield that protects everyone.

### Question 43

Used needles go straight into the special box - never touch or bend them.

### Question 44

Wash it right away and tell the person in charge immediately.

### Question 45

Once something wet and germy lands on the clean cloth, start fresh.

### Question 46

If the 'use by' date passed, get a fresh one.

### Question 47

You cannot take pictures of a patient's private care without permission.

### Question 48

Do not let others peek at the screen; sign out when done.

### Question 49

Let the person change alone behind a closed curtain.

### Question 50

Share only what is needed, not the whole story.

### Question 51

'Clean' means fewer germs; 'sterile' means zero germs.

### Question 52

The color-change tape shows the package went through the machine, like a stamp, but you still follow all the other rules.

### Question 53

A 'do not disturb' signal so people do not walk in.

### Question 54

Clean up the dirty one and make a fresh one.

### Question 55

Germs can slip through wet surfaces, so keep things dry.

### Question 56

If it hangs over the clean zone and touches the dirty table, it is no longer clean.

### Question 57

What happens in the exam room stays private.

### Question 58

Turn away and cover up so germs do not land on the clean area.

### Question 59

Give the clean zone its own space.

### Question 60

Hold your clean hands up where they cannot bump into dirty things.

### Question 61

If you are not sure, play it safe and get a new one.

### Question 62

If someone wants privacy or a helper, respect that.

### Question 63

Put private papers away where others cannot read them.

### Question 64

Tell them what to take off, then step out.

### Question 65

Your hands are not germ-free, so do not touch the clean inside.

### Question 66

Follow all the germ-free rules at once to keep the safe zone safe.

### Question 67

Fix the cover-up carefully without touching the clean zone, and tell someone.

### Question 68

Never touch a used needle - let the right person put it in the special box.

### Question 69

Even with gloves, wash your hands after taking them off.

### Question 70

Help start over with clean supplies when told.

### Question 71

The outside edge is always 'dirty' even if it looks clean.

### Question 72

If nobody watched the clean zone, it is no longer trusted.

### Question 73

Blood spills get cleaned the special safe way, not with bare hands.

### Question 74

Germs ride through wet fabric like water soaking through paper.

### Question 75

Even with clean gloves, only touch clean things.

### Question 76

Wear the full 'rain gear' when things might splash.

### Question 77

Wiping is 'cleaning,' not 'zero-germ.'

### Question 78

Speak up about everything you see wrong.

### Question 79

Talk about the case without names, in private.

### Question 80

Your info is shared only when needed for your care or with your OK.

### Question 81

Carry dirty cloths away from you and wash your hands after.

### Question 82

Do things in the right order: clean hands first, check packages, open carefully.

### Question 83

Take the time needed and keep them covered.

### Question 84

Skin gets cleaned but cannot be made totally germ-free.

### Question 85

Do not use the dirty area; tell the person in charge as soon as you can.
